result:
All checks pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 7/7 passing (the two "Unhandled exception" printouts in the output are expected 422 validation errors logged by the framework's error handler, not test failures).

**Root cause**: the route was registered as `posts.get('/archive/:date*', ...)`. Hono has no `:param*` syntax — its label parser (`node_modules/hono/dist/utils/url.js`) treats the whole thing as a literal param name `"date*"` that only ever matches a single path segment. That's exactly why `/posts/archive/2026/08` (two segments) 404'd, while `/posts/archive/2026` matched but populated a param key of `date*` instead of `date`, so `ArchiveParamSchema` (which expects `date`) saw it as missing and threw a 422.

**Fix**: `routes/web.ts` now registers `posts.get('/archive/:date{.+}', ...)`, Hono's actual syntax for a named param that can contain slashes. This captures both `2026` and `2026/08` (or `2026/8`) into a single `date` param exactly as `PostController.archive` and `ArchiveParamSchema` already expected, so no other code needed to change — the existing regex already validates months 1–12 and rejects out-of-range months with a 422, and `createdAt` was already stored via `toISOString()` (UTC), so the prefix-match comparison was already correct.

I added a `posts.archive` describe block to `tests/PostController.test.ts` covering: month lookup with/without a leading zero, year lookup, an empty period, and an out-of-range month returning 422 — using fixture posts created in 2010 (a year no seeder touches) so the assertions don't depend on the seeded/demo data.
